name: Band Clamshell
summary: A side-lying hip exercise using a resistance band looped around the thighs to strengthen the gluteal abductors and external rotators.

setup: Loop a resistance band around both legs, positioning it just above your knees.
Lie on your side on the floor with your head supported by your lower arm or a pad.
Bend your hips to about 45 degrees and your knees to about 90 degrees, stacking your hips, knees, and feet directly on top of each other.
steps: Keeping your feet glued together and your pelvis completely steady, rotate your top knee upward into the air against band resistance.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, focusing on a strong contraction in the outer glute.
Slowly lower the top knee back to touch the bottom knee while maintaining control against the band tension.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you lift the knee against the band tension; inhale as you lower back to the starting position.
cues: Squeeze the side of your hip at the top.

common_faults.fault: Rolling the pelvis backward during the lift to gain extra height.
common_faults.correction: Keep your pelvis perpendicular to the floor and only raise the knee as far as your hip can externally rotate without twisting your spine.

common_faults.fault: Separating the feet during the repetition.
common_faults.correction: Maintain light, continuous contact between the soles of your feet throughout the entire movement.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the band to snap the knee down quickly on the eccentric phase.
common_faults.correction: Resist the band tension and lower the knee smoothly over a two- to three-second count.
